draft.title: Energy transformations
card: Energy can change from one form to another. This change is called an energy transformation.
A torch changes chemical energy stored in its battery into light and thermal energy. A toaster changes electrical energy into thermal energy and a little light.
Many devices make more than one form of energy. The forms that are not the one we want are often thermal energy or sound.
Energy is not made or destroyed. The total amount of energy stays the same, and it only changes form or moves from place to place.
draft.remember: Energy changes form, but the total amount stays the same.

a.q: A student switches on a battery-powered fan. Which energy transformation takes place first in the battery as the fan starts?
a.why: A battery stores chemical energy and changes it into electrical energy to run the fan. The reverse order is tempting, but that would be the battery being charged, not used.
a.clue: Which form of energy is stored in a battery?

b.q: Priya says that when a candle burns away, its chemical energy is destroyed. Which statement about her claim is correct?
opts: Wrong, it changes into light and thermal energy
Wrong, it changes into more chemical energy
Right, the candle gets smaller so energy is lost
Right, the flame makes the energy disappear
b.why: Energy is not destroyed. The chemical energy in the wax changes into light and thermal energy. The candle shrinking is tempting evidence, but the energy has changed form, not vanished.
b.clue: Where does the energy go if it cannot be destroyed?

b.best: Wrong, it changes into light and thermal energy
